description:
JMAP-cf7p.4 (SSE GET /events) and JMAP-cf7p.5 (WS GET /ws) both need to broadcast RFC 8620 §7.4 StateChange events when the mounted MemoryBackends mutate. None of the 8 reference MemoryBackends currently expose a subscribe/notify API — grep for 'subscribe' / 'broadcast' / 'tokio::sync::broadcast' across mail/chat/calendars/tasks/contacts/filenode/sharing/metadata memory.rs files returns zero matches.

Two design forks, both surfaced at the boundary of the cf7p.4 bead body itself:

  (a) **Polling fallback**: testjig spawns a tokio interval task per backend that calls get_state for each tracked type every N ms (say 250 ms), diffs against the last seen state token, emits StateChange when anything changed. Pros: zero changes to any kit crate, fully self-contained in the testjig. Cons: 250 ms latency for state-change visibility (acceptable for tests, painful for interactive demos); per-type get_state calls scale O(types × backends × 1/interval) — for 8 backends × ~5 types each × 4 Hz = 160 calls/s on an idle jig.

  (b) **Subscription API on all 8 reference MemoryBackends**: add  (or similar) to each MemoryBackend, called once at registration; backends fire-and-forget broadcast on every state-counter increment. Pros: zero polling overhead, instant state change visibility. Cons: workspace-architectural decision per the canonical-templates rule — the change would land in jmap-mail-server (canonical) first and propagate to all 7 siblings; touches the cookie-cutter discipline.

Recommendation: option (a) for cf7p.4 + .5. The testjig posture is 'NOT FOR PRODUCTION'; 250 ms polling is fine for tests. Option (b) is a much larger change that should be scoped as its own workspace epic if anyone has a use case for it (downstream consumers that want push-grade latency from a real backend).

This bead exists to record the decision point. cf7p.4 + cf7p.5 should not be claimed by /do-beads until either (a) Mark explicitly authorizes the polling-fallback design (no human needed beyond the authorization) or (b) Mark files a sibling epic to add the subscribe API across all 8 backends.

Filing as human-labeled because it's a design fork the autonomous loop should not pre-decide.
title: Decision: SSE (cf7p.4) + WS (cf7p.5) need MemoryBackend subscribe API or polling
